title: Guitar and banjo players: Jim Lucas, Walter, Freddie Gould
summary: He discusses fingerpicking style, banjo player Jim Lucas who played with Rene, the blues picker Walter, and the crippled guitarist Freddie Gould.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I was wondering if you ever noticed, would they use a flat pick or would they use finger picks and thumb picks or all different kinds of things?

Well in that time, them fellows would use just their fingers. I see here lately now, I see them fellows with them picks, you know, them sideline picks, but them fellows way back then, I mean they'd just be picking that with their fingers. I mean they'd play it too. Old fellow Jim Lucas, he used to play some guitar, played banjo, but he played in bands and he used to play with Rene and all them fellas. Is he still around? Hmm? Is he still around? No, Jim Lucas, he died, he been dead. He was a good banjo player, guitar player too. He played most with all the bands.
You can hardly find a good blues picker like you used to. There's very few of them around.

Like guitar? Yeah. I believe Walter was about the only one, I mean, you know, picking the blues. He can play the blues there, he really can, you know, picking them on that style, you see. But most of them fellas that was playing during that time, I mean, they, they, now they had a fella down to him. I could play any of them, playing the guitar, blues and everything. He's crippled now. His name is Freddie. Freddie. He's a lottery vendor.
He lived down at Nightwars. Freddie. Freddie Gould. Freddie Gould. Freddie Gould. I mean, he'd play high school.
